findings.comment: License agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement required if landscaping is within electric easement areas. Electric easement boundaries are not shown on Landscape Plan, and license agreement documentation is not evident in current submittal.
findings.observation: Plat (Sheet 2) shows 5-foot electric easements along northern and southern boundaries. Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) does not show electric easement boundaries. No license agreement documentation evident in current submittal. Grouping guidance notes license agreements are administrative documents that may not be attached at early stages but must be verified before occupancy.
findings.reasoning: If landscaping within electric easements, UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement. Plans do not show easement boundaries coordinated with Landscape Plan, and agreement documentation not evident in current submittal. Unclear whether landscaping is within easements and whether agreement has been obtained.

findings.comment: Obtain a License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement before installing any landscaping, trees, irrigation, or plantings within electric easement areas. Provide executed copy with final site plan submittal or reference execution in a plan note.
findings.observation: Review of all available site plan documents and supplementary documents (including Master Comment Report) reveals no executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement for landscaping, trees, or irrigation within electric easement areas. The Master Comment Report (Electric Review section) references Austin Energy preliminary design requirements including UCM § 1.10.10.3, which requires a License Agreement before installing landscaping in electric easement areas. No such agreement is attached to the plans, referenced in any plan notes, or mentioned in any accompanying documentation. Sheet 31 shows trees proposed in areas where electric easements exist (per property records), but there is no evidence of the required license agreement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 explicitly requires that 'a License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement is required before installing landscaping, trees, irrigation, or plantings that might obstruct access to Austin Energy facilities within electric easement areas. The agreement must be obtained and filed before the activity occurs.' The absence of this license agreement documentation on or with the site plan is a deficiency. While license agreements are administrative documents that may be obtained after plan approval, the applicant must provide evidence that the requirement has been addressed (or provide the executed agreement).

findings.comment: Unable to verify whether proposed trees block truck access to transformers or equipment set-up areas due to lack of electrical infrastructure and access route coordination on Landscape Plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows transformer locations throughout site. Sheet 31 shows proposed trees but does not coordinate with transformer locations or equipment access requirements. Cannot assess whether proposed plantings obstruct access without electrical infrastructure shown on Landscape Plan.
findings.reasoning: Cannot verify access compliance without showing transformer locations and required turning radii/access clearances coordinated with proposed tree locations on Landscape Plan.

findings.comment: Show transformer locations and required truck access routes on the landscape plan. Verify no trees block access lanes or turning radii required for Austin Energy service vehicles (typical 40-50 ft turning radius for bucket trucks).
applicableAreas: Transformer locations and access routes throughout site
findings.observation: Transformer pad locations from Sheet 21 and access routes from Sheet 9 (Site Plan) are not overlaid on the landscape plan (Sheet 31). Without this coordination, it cannot be verified that proposed trees do not obstruct access routes or turning radii for bucket trucks used to service transformers and Austin Energy equipment.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 states that landscaping must not restrict Austin Energy personnel and equipment access. The landscape plan must show transformer locations and access requirements to demonstrate compliance. The absence of this coordination indicates non-compliance with the access requirement.

findings.comment: Trees and vegetation are shown within the southern and eastern 5' electric easement areas without documentation of a license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement. Provide a copy of the executed license agreement 'obtained from and filed with Austin Energy Public Involvement' authorizing landscaping and irrigation within these easements, or relocate all landscaping outside the easement boundaries.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts multiple tree and vegetation symbols (circles with branching patterns indicating trees) directly within the southern 5' electric easement along the southern property line and within the eastern 5' electric easement along the eastern property line. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) confirms tree placement with symbols labeled 'M' (Mitigation Trees), 'PL' (Parking Lot Trees), and 'P' (Parking Buffer Point Trees) positioned adjacent to or within these easement areas. The Landscape Plan contains 'IRRIGATION NOTES' but does not reference any license agreement from Austin Energy. The site plan notes on Sheet 3 contain no statement confirming that a license agreement has been 'obtained from and filed with' Austin Energy Public Involvement. Site plan notes use general language about easement provision but do not specifically confirm an executed license agreement for landscaping/irrigation within the electric easements.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 is explicit and unambiguous: 'Landscaping and irrigation systems [are] permissible within easements only with license agreement obtained from and filed with Austin Energy Public Involvement.' The regulatory standard uses the exact phrase 'obtained from and filed with'—not 'to be obtained' and not 'requested.' The site plan shows landscaping (trees) within easement boundaries but provides no documentation of an executed license agreement. The burden of demonstrating compliance is on the applicant. Missing executed license agreement documentation is grounds for deficiency, as this can result in certificate of occupancy holds and Austin Energy removal of non-compliant landscaping at the owner's cost.

findings.comment: The detention pond with required vegetation is located within the 5' Electric Easement but no executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement is documented on the plans. Obtain and file license agreement with Austin Energy authorizing landscaping and vegetation within the easement, or relocate pond outside easement boundary.
applicableAreas: Biofiltration/detention pond area and eastern property boundary within 5' Electric Easement
findings.observation: Sheet 16 (Biofiltration-Detention Pond Profiles) maintenance requirements specify: 'No unvegetated area shall exceed ten (10) square feet. This performance requirement applies to the entire pond including the pond bottom, side slopes, and areas adjacent to the pond.' The pond requires 95% vegetative cover per biweekly maintenance inspections in the first growing season. Vision analysis of Sheet 9 confirmed the pond is located within the 5' Electric Easement along the eastern boundary. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows the pond area and adjacent landscape features but contains no indication of a license agreement with Austin Energy Public Involvement. No document references or site plan notes state 'obtained from and filed with Austin Energy Public Involvement' regarding landscaping authorization within the easement. The absence of a filed license agreement is the deficiency.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires: 'A license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement is required before installing any landscaping or irrigation that might obstruct access to facilities within electric easements.' The grouping description clarifies: 'Plans showing landscaping within easements must demonstrate the license agreement has been "obtained from and filed with" Austin Energy Public Involvement—not "to be obtained." Missing license agreements result in certificate of occupancy holds.' The detention pond's required vegetation (95% cover) constitutes landscaping within the electric easement. The submitted plans provide no evidence that an executed license agreement has been obtained from and filed with Austin Energy Public Involvement.

findings.comment: Retaining walls, fences, landscaping, and other improvements within the electric easements obstruct required 24/7 vehicular maintenance access for Austin Energy personnel and equipment. Ensure that easement areas remain completely clear of all obstructions and maintain a continuous, unobstructed access corridor at least 12 feet wide within the easement for Austin Energy maintenance activities.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts concrete retaining walls, a wood fence, driveways, and sidewalks located within or directly overlapping the southern and eastern 5' electric easement boundaries. These physical structures create barriers and obstructions to the easement area. Retaining walls run parallel to easement boundaries at the perimeter, creating access restrictions. The wood fence is drawn directly within the eastern 5' easement area. Driveways and sidewalks, while potentially providing some access routes, are designed for pedestrian and vehicle traffic to/from buildings rather than maintenance access for Austin Energy personnel and equipment. No dimensions or callout indicate that a clear, continuous, drivable maintenance corridor is maintained within or adjacent to these easements. The plan shows landscaping (trees) also positioned within easement areas, further reducing open access.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 states that landscaping within easements is permitted only 'if landscaping does not restrict 24/7 access.' The phrase is also reinforced in the general prohibition language emphasizing that Austin Energy must maintain '24-hour unimpeded access to all electric facilities.' Retaining walls and fences are structures that inherently restrict access; trees and vegetation also impede equipment movement. The site plan shows these features within the easement boundaries, and there is no notation, callout, or specification stating that a 24/7 maintenance access corridor is maintained free of obstruction. The presence of these features within the easement area violates the requirement for unrestricted access.

findings.comment: The detention pond with required vegetation and concrete retaining walls within the 5' Electric Easement obstructs required 24/7 vehicular access for Austin Energy maintenance. Relocate pond outside the easement or demonstrate 24-foot minimum clear drivable surface for maintenance vehicle access across the easement width.
applicableAreas: 5' Electric Easement along eastern property boundary
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 9 confirms the detention pond retaining wall is within the 5' Electric Easement. Sheet 16 specifies the pond requires vegetation maintenance with 95% cover and detailed biweekly and routine maintenance. Vision analysis of Sheet 31 shows trees in the eastern boundary area near the pond. The concrete retaining wall physically encloses the pond area. While the landscape plan shows some access routes and a maintenance gate (per Sheet 16 details), the required vegetation within the pond and the concrete retaining wall infrastructure would obstruct free vehicular access for Austin Energy maintenance trucks and equipment to traverse the easement. The retaining wall and pond infrastructure are permanent features that occupy and restrict the 24/7 vehicular access corridor.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires that 'landscaping within easements must maintain 24/7 vehicular access for Austin Energy personnel and equipment.' A concrete retaining wall enclosing a pond, combined with required dense vegetation (95% cover), creates a physical obstruction preventing free vehicular access across the easement. The maintenance requirements (routine vegetation trimming, inspections, replacement) also require Austin Energy to navigate around or within the landscaped pond area. This setup does not maintain unobstructed access.

findings.comment: Trees planted within the southern 5-foot electric easement on the landscape plan without evidence of a required Austin Energy Public Involvement license agreement. A license agreement must be obtained before installing landscaping or trees within electric easements per UCM § 1.10.10.3.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) clearly depicts a 5-foot electric easement running along the southern property boundary, labeled '5' Elec. Easement' with plat references (Vol. 69, Pg. 14 and Vol. 73, Pg. 76). Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows extensive tree plantings throughout the site, including a group of three proposed trees located along the southeastern section of the property boundary directly over the overhead electric line (OHE). Measurement analysis of Sheet 31 indicates these trees are positioned approximately 0.5 feet from the southern property line, which places them at or within the 5-foot electric easement boundary. The consolidated site plan application (supplementary document) indicates 'No' response to the question 'Will a License Agreement Application be submitted for this project?' No Austin Energy Public Involvement license agreement is referenced or attached to the site plan documents.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires a license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement before installing landscaping, trees, irrigation, or utility-compatible plantings within electric easement areas. The proposed trees positioned at the southern property boundary are at or within the 5-foot electric easement, as confirmed by both the easement boundary shown on Sheet 9 and the measured position of trees on Sheet 31 (approximately 0.5 feet from property line). The absence of any reference to an executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement, combined with the presence of proposed plantings within the easement area, constitutes non-compliance with UCM § 1.10.10.3. The applicant must either: (1) demonstrate through survey certification that all proposed trees are located outside the 5-foot easement boundary, or (2) provide evidence of an executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement authorizing the landscaping within the easement.

findings.comment: License agreement not obtained from Austin Energy Public Involvement for landscaping and trees proposed within electric easements. Multiple trees are plotted within or adjacent to electric easement boundaries on the southern and northern property lines. Prior to final approval, applicant must obtain a license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement authorizing vegetation placement within the easement areas, or remove/relocate trees outside easement boundaries.
applicableAreas: Northern property boundary near overhead electric line
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows multiple trees proposed directly on or immediately adjacent to the overhead electric (OHE) easement line on the southern property boundary. Visual analysis identified tree symbols plotted within and parallel to the dashed OHE line, indicating vegetation placement within the electric easement footprint. Additionally, trees are proposed at the northern property boundary where the 5-foot historic electric easement exists. The landscape plan contains irrigation notes but no reference to Austin Energy license agreements, Austin Energy coordination, or acknowledgment of requirements for landscaping within electric easement areas. No separate license agreement document is evident in supplementary documents.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 explicitly requires a license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement before installing landscaping, trees, irrigation, or utility-compatible plantings that might obstruct Austin Energy's access to facilities within electric easement areas. The visual evidence of trees plotted within the overhead electric easement boundaries triggers this requirement. The applicant cannot simply plant within easement areas; prior authorization is mandatory. The absence of (1) tree/landscape restrictions on the landscape plan, (2) a license agreement document, or (3) any acknowledgment of this requirement on either the landscape or general notes sheets indicates non-compliance. UCM § 1.10.10.3 further states that Austin Energy reserves the right to remove any obstruction without fault, and property owners are responsible for all costs.

findings.comment: Trees and landscaping proposed within or immediately adjacent to underground and overhead electric easement areas without documented license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement
applicableAreas: Landscape areas adjacent to underground electric lines (Street Yard areas and southern property boundary); areas adjacent to overhead electric line locations

documentReferences.label: Master Comment Report - Electric Review (UCM § 1.10.10.3 & 4 referenced as design criteria)

findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) vision analysis found: 'Several proposed trees (indicated by circles with crosses/symbols inside) are shown directly overlapping or planted immediately adjacent to the overhead electric line...along the bottom edge of the property' and 'Proposed trees within the shaded Street Yard area...on the left side of the property are situated near the underground electric lines.' The landscape plan legend and blocks identify trees by type (SY = Street Yard Tree, PL = Parking Lot Tree, M = Mitigation Tree, P = Parking Buffer Point Tree) but do NOT include any callouts, notes, or references to license agreements from Austin Energy Public Involvement. The Sheet 31 vision analysis explicitly states: 'Specific irrigation system components (such as sprinklers, irrigation heads, or lateral lines) are not shown on this plan' and 'A thorough review of all text on the page...reveals no callouts or notes mentioning license agreements or coordination with Austin Energy Public Involvement.' No license agreement plan sheet is referenced. The Master Comment Report Electric Review section lists UCM § 1.10.10.3 & 4 (Customer Activity in Utility Easements - Landscaping & Trees) as applicable design criteria for Austin Energy review, indicating this is a known coordination requirement, yet no executed license agreement is provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 explicitly requires that 'a license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement must be obtained before installing landscaping, trees, irrigation, or utility-compatible plantings that might in any way obstruct Austin Energy's access to facilities within electric easement areas.' The presence of trees and landscaping near (and potentially within) electric easement areas without a documented license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement constitutes non-compliance. The grouping guidance states: 'License agreements are also required...for any construction or improvements within transmission easements (requiring City Law Department encroachment agreement)' and that reviewers should 'Check: Landscape plan and irrigation plan against electric easement boundaries.' Sheet 31 shows trees adjacent to electric infrastructure. No license agreement is documented. The Master Comment Report indicates Austin Energy HAS reviewed this aspect (per UCM § 1.10.10.3 & 4 reference), but the lack of a visible executed or referenced license agreement on the site plan constitutes a deficiency.

findings.comment: No License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement is evident for trees/landscaping proposed within electric easements. Before installation of any landscaping, irrigation, or trees within electric easement areas, obtain License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement and provide copy to City. Add plan note: 'License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement obtained prior to installation of landscaping within electric easement areas' [date/agreement number to be inserted].
applicableAreas: Electric easement areas (5' Electric Easements per Mecey Subdivision plat)
findings.observation: Reviewed all landscape and supplementary documents for evidence of a License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement for trees proposed within electric easements. Facts.md identifies two electric easements on the Mecey Subdivision plat: '5' Electric Easements (×2)' (Document Ref: Travis County Doc 73/76, Case C8S-75-160). Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows trees (M for mitigation) distributed around the site perimeter, some of which visually appear to fall within or adjacent to easement areas based on the site layout. However, Sheet 31 does not display easement boundaries overlaid with the landscape plan, making it difficult to determine precisely which trees fall within easement areas from the landscape plan alone. More critically, the landscape plans, site plans, and supplementary documents contain NO reference to a License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement, NO plan notes stating 'License Agreement obtained from Austin Energy Public Involvement,' and NO attached license agreement documentation. Per grouping guidance: 'License agreements are administrative documents that may not be attached at early review stages. Flag requirement for verification before certificate of occupancy.' However, per UCM § 1.10.10.3, the agreement must be 'obtained and filed before the activity occurs,' and missing license agreements result in certificate of occupancy holds.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires that before landscaping, trees, irrigation, or plantings are installed within electric easement areas, a License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement must be obtained and filed. The applicant's responsibility at site plan stage is to demonstrate awareness of this requirement through either (a) a reference to an obtained license agreement (date and agreement number), or (b) a plan note committing to obtain the agreement before construction. Without such documentation, the reviewer cannot confirm the requirement will be met. The presence of proposed trees within or likely within electric easement areas, combined with the complete absence of license agreement documentation, constitutes a deficiency. The grouping guidance acknowledges license agreements may not be attached at early review but flags for verification—this is that flag. The applicant must either provide evidence of a license agreement or add a plan note committing to obtain one before construction/installation of any landscaping within the electric easements.

findings.comment: Tree plantings and landscaping are shown within 5-foot electric easements on north, south, and east boundaries without documented evidence of executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement. Provide executed license agreement letter from Austin Energy Public Involvement confirming that landscaping/irrigation within the easement has been 'obtained from and filed with' the City (not 'to be obtained'). Agreement must be attached to site plan submittal prior to approval.
applicableAreas: Tree plantings within 5-foot electric easements on northern, eastern, and southern property boundaries
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows tree plantings (marked with symbols including 'M' for mitigation trees, 'SY' for street yard trees, 'PL' for parking lot trees) positioned directly adjacent to and overlapping the property boundary lines on the north, south, and east sides of the site. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts 5-foot electric easements running along these same property boundaries: '5' Electric Easement' on the south, '5' Electric Easement' on the east (lower portion), and '5' P.U.E.' on the north. The tree plantings shown on the landscape plan, being placed at or within the property boundary, fall within the 5-foot easement widths. No notes, callouts, or attached documentation on either the landscape plan or site plan reference an executed license agreement obtained from and filed with Austin Energy Public Involvement. The landscape plan's 'IRRIGATION NOTES' section discusses TCEQ Chapter 344 compliance but makes no reference to an easement license agreement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 states that landscaping and irrigation are permissible within electric easements only with a license agreement obtained from and filed with Austin Energy Public Involvement. The checklist specifically requires that plans demonstrate the license agreement has been 'obtained from and filed with' Austin Energy—not to be obtained. The site plan notes in Sheet 9 do not confirm that this agreement exists; instead, note d mentions 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date,' which acknowledges potential future easement constraints but does not address current compliance. Without documented evidence of the executed license agreement, the landscaping plantings shown within the easements cannot be approved. This is a certificate of occupancy hold item per the grouping guidance.

findings.comment: Tree plantings shown within electric easements would obstruct 24/7 vehicular access required for Austin Energy maintenance. Relocate all trees and landscaping outside the 5-foot electric easement boundaries to maintain unobstructed access corridor, or provide engineer certification that design maintains minimum 12-foot clear width for maintenance vehicle access along entire easement length. Additionally, obtain and file executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement per UCM § 1.10.10.3.
applicableAreas: Tree plantings and landscaping within 5-foot electric easements on property perimeters
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) depicts tree plantings positioned within the 5-foot electric easements running along the north, south, and east property boundaries. Trees are shown with canopy symbols (circles) that extend several feet from the trunk location. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows that these easements run the full length of these property lines. The placement of trees with mature canopies within these easement corridors would create physical obstructions that would prevent unrestricted vehicular access for Austin Energy maintenance personnel and equipment. Easement widths (5 feet) are minimal; tree canopies, trunks, and root systems would occupy much of this width, leaving insufficient space for a maintenance vehicle to traverse the easement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires that landscaping within electric easements be positioned such that it does not restrict 24/7 vehicular access for Austin Energy personnel and equipment. The fundamental purpose of an electric easement is to provide Austin Energy with unrestricted access for construction, operation, maintenance, and repair of electric facilities. Tree plantings shown within the 5-foot easement corridors, with typical canopy spreads of 20-40+ feet (varying by species), would substantially obstruct this required access. Even if a license agreement were in place (which it is not, per EL-5.11), landscaping must be designed to maintain unobstructed access. The current landscape plan does not demonstrate this; trees are shown directly within the easement boundaries.
